Implementation Plan

Planning ref: `6d3930f9f942b2444e458b9d9acd8d58865924d1` on `orchestrator/project-3496` (matches integration-branch metadata).

Clarification mapping: no `Q<ID>` batch was issued; `/answer [auto-answered-by-orchestrator]` only confirmed continuation, so the issue is sufficiently specified for planning.

Files likely to change
- Prompt-render pipeline:
  - `scripts/render_prompt.py`
  - `scripts/render_prompt.sh`
  - `scripts/assemble_prompt.sh`
- Shared prompt assets:
  - `prompts/_prelude_common.txt` (if its include coverage needs adjustment)
  - new checked-in persona source, preferably `prompts/_prelude_role_persona.txt` (or an equivalently strict checked-in file)
- Missing template-backed prompt files (7 currently absent from `prompts/_templates/`):
  - `prompts/_templates/mode-clarify-respond.txt`
  - `prompts/_templates/mode-extract-learnings.txt`
  - `prompts/_templates/mode-security-audit.txt`
  - `prompts/_templates/mode-validate-generate.txt`
  - `prompts/_templates/mode-workflow-analysis.txt`
  - `prompts/_templates/mode-workflow-api-redundancy.txt`
  - `prompts/_templates/mode-workflow-audit.txt`
- Isolated-workspace/bootstrap surfaces that stage prompt assets:
  - `.github/workflows/orchestrate.yml`
  - `.github/workflows/orchestrate_clarify_respond.yml`
  - `.github/workflows/validate.yml`
  - `scripts/stage_workflow_support.sh`
  - `agents.md` if the prompt-assembly architecture note changes materially
- Regression/contract tests:
  - `tests/test_assemble_prompt.py`
  - `tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py`
  - `tests/test_render_prompt_core_modes.py`
  - `tests/test_render_prompt_validate_analytics_modes.py`
  - `tests/test_validate_semble_contract.py`
  - `tests/test_validate_workflow_validate_bootstrap.py`
  - `tests/test_workflow_overlay_orchestrator.py`
  - `tests/test_review_rb_judge_reference_staging.py`

Functions/modules to implement
- Restore the shared-prelude assembly path end-to-end:
  - add a real assembly mode to `render_prompt.py` (or equivalent backend behavior) so `assemble_prompt.sh` no longer calls an unsupported CLI
  - re-enable flag-gated assembly in `render_prompt.sh` so `PROMPT_PRELUDE_REFACTOR_ENABLED=true` actually uses `_templates/<mode>.txt`, while `false` stays on legacy flat prompts
- Add strict template parsing/validation:
  - reject unsupported expressions like `{{FOO|lower}}`
  - fail on unknown filters/tags/unsupported template syntax before emitting prompt output
  - preserve the current contract/reference hydration behavior for supported placeholders
- Move persona sourcing to a checked-in asset:
  - load persona text from a checked-in prompt fragment/mapping instead of Python-only logic (or, on this ref, the currently missing logic)
  - keep the existing `PROMPT_PERSONA_PREFIX_ENABLED` compatibility semantics
- Complete template migration for the live prompt inventory:
  - derive from the existing pattern in `prompts/_templates/mode-validate-discover.txt`
  - keep each new template byte-stable with its legacy `prompts/mode-*.txt` body after assembly
- Replace the hand-maintained migrated list in `tests/test_assemble_prompt.py` with live inventory discovery over `prompts/mode-*.txt`, then assert:
  - every active mode prompt has a corresponding template
  - assembled output matches the legacy file bytes
  - flag-off rendering still returns the legacy file unchanged
- Update support-bundle staging so template/prelude/persona assets exist anywhere prompts are rendered outside the full repo root

Data structures affected
- Active prompt inventory: 28 live `prompts/mode-*.txt` files, 21 template-backed today, 7 missing
- Checked-in mode→persona source (new file or equivalent checked-in mapping)
- Staged prompt-asset lists in workflow manifests/support-bundle helpers
- No DB/schema/API payload changes outside the internal prompt-render toolchain

API/interface changes
- `scripts/render_prompt.py` gains a supported assembly entrypoint (`--assemble-only` or equivalent)
- `scripts/render_prompt.sh` regains meaningful `PROMPT_PRELUDE_REFACTOR_ENABLED` behavior
- Unsupported template syntax becomes a hard render failure instead of pass-through output
- `PROMPT_PERSONA_PREFIX_ENABLED` should remain backward-compatible, but its content source moves to checked-in prompt assets

Risks and edge cases
- Conflict with issue line references: on this ref, `scripts/render_prompt.sh` is only 144 lines and has no assembly-flag branch; the branch is more regressed than the issue text suggests.
- `scripts/assemble_prompt.sh` currently fails because it passes `--assemble-only` to a parser that does not accept it; `tests/test_assemble_prompt.py` is already red on this ref.
- The issue cites hard-coded persona logic in `scripts/render_prompt.py`, but the current file has no persona handling at all; `tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py` is already red on the expected persona-prefix behavior.
- `mode-validate-self-heal` and the Semble/Serena contract tests intentionally preserve literal placeholder examples; strict rendering must keep those literals via raw blocks or equivalent handling.
- Reusing Jinja2 directly is attractive because `scripts/render_validation_templates.py` already uses `StrictUndefined`, but prompt rendering runs in workflows that do not currently provision Jinja2 outside validate/CI. Either keep the prompt assembler dependency-free or update runtime provisioning/bootstrap wherever `render_prompt.sh` is used.
- Only some prompt-render call sites use isolated support bundles; those bundles must stage the new template/prelude/persona assets or flag-on renders will fail there while still passing in source-repo runs.

Testing considerations
- Targeted renderer suite:
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_assemble_prompt.py`
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_render_prompt_foundation.py`
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_render_prompt_core_modes.py`
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_render_prompt_validate_analytics_modes.py`
- Bootstrap/staging regressions:
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_validate_semble_contract.py`
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_validate_workflow_validate_bootstrap.py`
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_workflow_overlay_orchestrator.py`
  - `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_review_rb_judge_reference_staging.py`
- Add/extend explicit regressions for:
  - `{{FOO|lower}}` failing closed
  - flag-off rendering returning legacy bytes
  - full-inventory template coverage, not a static allowlist

Implementation-time estimate: 55 minutes
Scope-mode: Selective Expansion
Reuse-audit: extends the existing template-backed prompt pattern in `prompts/_templates/mode-validate-discover.txt` and the strict-template approach already used by `scripts/render_validation_templates.py`.
Scope-mode justification: the smallest correct fix is broader than a single renderer patch because the approved Phase O scope requires all active mode prompts, strict render failures, checked-in persona sourcing, and consumer/support-bundle coverage together. Stopping at `render_prompt.py`/`test_assemble_prompt.py` would leave the rollout partial and still broken in isolated workspaces, so the safe implementation must include the repetitive template/staging/test updates inside this bounded subsystem.

Assumptions made
- All 28 current `prompts/mode-*.txt` files are still active because no prompt is marked retired on this ref.
- The preferred checked-in persona source is the planned `prompts/_prelude_role_persona.txt` unless an equivalent checked-in mapping yields the same stricter regression coverage with less bootstrap churn.

Missing-context notes
- The issue’s cited `render_prompt.sh` / `render_prompt.py` line ranges do not match the checked-out branch; this plan follows the live codebase truth on `orchestrator/project-3496`.

PLAN_SELF_CHECK: WARNING: the checked-out branch is more regressed than the issue text implies (`--assemble-only` missing, assembly flag unwired, persona logic absent), so the implementation must treat the current codebase—not the stale line references—as the source of truth.
